raw_response:
Aiya, you want me to tell you what I'm doing this year? Okay, let me think.

I'm 68 now, been on this 4.5 mu my whole adult life — 25 years since I took it over. My wife helps a little, but our son works in the city now, only comes back for the busy weeks. So it's mostly me. Two mouths at home, plus we eat some of our own wheat flour.

The land is split — I keep about 2.5 mu for wheat-maize rotation on the better plot, and the other 2 mu also does wheat-maize because that's just how everyone around here does it. Cotton? No, too much work picking, my back can't do it anymore. Wheat and maize you can let the combine do the hard part.

**Wheat (winter):**
I already planted in mid-October last fall — that's the normal time, any later and the frost gets the seedlings. I used the seed I bought from the agricultural supply shop, same variety as my neighbor Old Zhang uses, about 40 yuan of seed per mu. I sowed maybe 15 kg seed per mu, a little heavy because I'm old and I'd rather have thick seedlings than thin ones.

Before planting I put down one bag of compound fertilizer (the 15-15-15 kind) per mu, that's about 50 kg. Cost me around 150 yuan a bag. In spring, when the wheat greens up and starts jointing — around March, when the ground thaws — I'll topdress with urea, about 15 kg per mu. One bag of urea is enough for 3 mu roughly.

Irrigation — I'll water at least three times: once in winter before the ground freezes hard (I already did that), once at green-up, once at jointing. Maybe a fourth at grain-filling if it's dry. The well is shared with my neighbors, we take turns, costs about 40 yuan per mu each time for the electricity. Harvest will be early June, I hire the combine — 50 yuan per mu, done in an hour. Much better than cutting by hand like when I was young.

Yield? Last year I got about 400 kg per mu, year before was 420. I expect similar. Not 500 like the big farms, but steady.

**Maize (summer):**
Right after wheat harvest, no time to waste — maybe 3 days between combine and planting. I'll hire the seeder (no-till, just drill into the wheat stubble), 30 yuan per mu. Seed is the hybrid kind from the shop, Zhengdan or Xianyu, about 50 yuan per mu.

Base fertilizer with the seed — one bag compound per mu again. Then I topdress once at the big-trumpet stage (大喇叭口期), maybe 15 kg urea per mu. Don't need as much as wheat I find — maize uses what's left in the soil from wheat.

Irrigation — maize needs less, usually 1-2 times if the summer rain isn't enough. If July and August rain well, I might not irrigate at all. Saves money.

Pesticide — I spray herbicide once after planting (atrazine, the regular one) and maybe one time for corn borer if I see them. Not much else. 

Harvest late September, combine again.

Yield — around 420-450 kg per mu usually.

**My thinking overall:**
I'm not trying to get the highest yield — I'm trying to not lose money and have enough grain at home. I stick with what I know. My neighbor tried to reduce fertilizer by half two years ago, his wheat was thin and yellow, he regretted it. So I keep my two bags (one base, one topdress). If I put less, I'm afraid; if I put more, it's wasted money. One bag compound plus some urea — that's what works for me.

Cash is always tight. My old-age pension helps, and our son sends some money, but I try not to spend more than 500-600 yuan per mu on inputs total across both crops.
